title: Heidi D NDE 1072
content:
I was seven years old and was on a bike hike with my two older sisters and a couple of their friends. It was a Sunday. We had ridden what I thought was a long way away from home. I had to borrow a bike from one of my sister's friends. We were going down a steep hill. I remember seeing a sign that said 'seven percent downgrade next two miles'. After starting on this hill, I realized that this bike was one where the pedals kept going as long as the bike was moving and I couldn't catch my brakes. I yelled out to my sister Kelly who was in front of me and told her that I couldn't catch my brakes and I was going too fast. She yelled back to me, 'Just put your feet out, and hold your breath and go!' I was so winded trying to keep up with my pedals that when I did just that - I held my breath - I passed out. I remember seeing my bike swerving back and forth. (I learned later that I crashed into a rock wall.) Next thing I remember was a total feeling of happiness and peace. I remember floating above a field of blue and yellow lupines. There aren't really words to describe the amount of joy I felt. I remember looking to the right and seeing green rolling hills. The colors were so brilliant and the air seemed perfect. Then I looked to my left and I saw me in the back of a red Jeep laid out behind the back seat. I saw my sister Kelly sitting in the back seat sobbing and shaking me asking me to please wake up. I distinctly remember the smell of vomit while I was looking down on myself. Then I remember pain. I was back in my body. I had vomited on myself. I remember looking at my sister thinking why did you make me come back?!? I guess I passed out again. The next thing I remember was looking down on myself again. This time we are in front of my house. My mom and dad were talking and there was a small crowd of people standing behind them. My mom ripped my shirt off and I remember seeing the boy I had a crush on standing in the crowd. I was telling my mom, 'Don't let Jay see my boobies.' My next memory was while they were wheeling me down the hallway at the hospital towards the emergency room. My mom was crying because she was worried that I had not regained consciousness yet. She was wearing a white crochet shawl with pink roses on it. My next memory was waking up in a hospital room with the most massive headache of my life. Every time I tried to sit up, I passed out. I remember asking mom where her shawl was. She looked at me funny and told me that it was in the closet because I had thrown up on it. 'How did you know I had it on?' she asked. I simply told her, 'I saw it.' It was years later that I learned that my memories were either Near Death Experience or out of body experience. I don't share the story very often. I remember the details like it happened yesterday.

boundary_and_return.return_method_other_detail: Abrupt return associated with “Then I remember pain. I was back in my body.” Later reports passing out again and re-separating.

context.nde_cause_other_detail: Bike crash after passing out going down a steep hill; later learned she “crashed into a rock wall.”

stage_sequence.elements_other_detail: Two separate OBEs: (1) floating over lupines/rolling hills and seeing self in a red Jeep; (2) looking down on self again in front of her house, then later hospital hallway observations.
stage_sequence.sequence_variation_description: OBE with peaceful landscape and veridical observations; return to body with pain; later passes out again and repeats OBE/observations.
stage_sequence.repeated_stage_detail: Repeated out-of-body viewing (“I guess I passed out again… looking down on myself again.”).

unique_elements.nonstandard_elements: Strong sensory detail during OBE including “smell of vomit” while viewing her body; concern about modesty while unconscious (“Don’t let Jay see my boobies.”).
unique_elements.notable_quotes: “There aren't really words to describe the amount of joy I felt.” / “Then I remember pain. I was back in my body.” / “How did you know I had it on?… I simply told her, ‘I saw it.’”
